newsitem.title: USA: FBI warns of potential conflicts of interest in fund-raising inquiry-Post.
newsitem.headline: FBI warns of potential conflicts of interest in fund-raising inquiry-Post.

text.p: FBI director Louis Freeh advised Attorney General Janet Reno that early evidence suggesting White House involvement in the Democratic Party fund-raising scandal should warrant appointment of an independent counsel, the Washington Post reported Wednesday.
Quoting unidentified government officials, the newspaper said Freeh made his recommendation to Reno orally as part of an FBI analysis of the evidence in the fund-raising scandal.
He did so, the officials said, after concluding that the Justice Department faced a possible conflict of interest in investigating the actions of several close aides to President Clinton.
Reno, however, decided on April 14 to follow the advice of other Justice Department officials who said an independent counsel was unnecessary.
The Post said Freeh's analysis concluded that evidence developed by the Justice Department task force could "lead to individuals who helped reelect the president."
The officials, who declined to say exactly when Freeh's recommendation was made, emphasised that his analysis was based on an interpretation of the facts, not the probe's political ramifications.

"There is no sense of an impasse between the director and the attorney general, a Justice Department source told the Post. "It is not a huge conflict." The official said Freeh did not try to force his view on Reno, who also was soliciting advice from career prosecutors in the Justice Department's criminal division.
